Your predecessor asked me once whether I believed in the reservoirs. I said belief was irregular. He laughed. I have not been laughed at since. You will find I have missed it.
Do you believe in the reservoirs?
"I believe in the pound. It is there every morning. That is enough belief for an auditor."
Laugh
You laugh. She almost does. It is the closest thing to a smile at the summit.
You look tired. I've got a thing for tired. Cargo. Hullfolk recipe, mostly legal. One cup and you'll turn paddles till dawn. Two and you'll see the river. Want one?
One cup
It tastes of reed and iron. You turn paddles till dawn. You do not see the river.
What river?
"Figure of speech. The old man's. Forget it." She does not forget you asked.
The old man says I'm going to end up like him. On a bollard, remembering. I'd rather end up in Sorrel with money. He'd rather I ended up here with a song. You're the tiebreaker. Pick.
Sorrel, with money
"Right answer. Wrong, but right."
Here, with a song
"You've been talking to him." She is not as annoyed as she sounds.
Fine. You saw me at the sluice house. I wasn't going in. I was seeing if anyone else was. Someone else was. Not Company. Not you. I don't know who. That's new.
Watch it with me
Two nights in the reeds. On the second, a lamp, and a woman's coat. Vosk.
Stay away from it
"You first."

Mirren Dray's the only townie who talks to me straight. She asked me what I know about her father. I know a bit. I haven't told her. I'm asking you if I should, because you're the only other one who's straight.
Tell her
She tells her. Mirren comes to the paddles with red eyes and works a double watch.
Not yet; tell me first
"He came to the Reach. Asked the old man about the hill. Went in. Didn't come out. That's it. That's all."

No jokes. Solas's men want the reed cargo doubled and they've stopped saying please. I said I'd think. If I stop, they'll find someone who won't stop, and that someone won't be careful. If I don't stop, I'm what the old man thinks I am.
Stop; I'll deal with Solas
"You'll deal with Solas. Right. I'd like to watch that." She stops.
Be careful; don't stop
"Careful. Yes. I'm always careful." She is, mostly.

I've learned the song. All of it. Don't tell the old man. He thinks I don't listen. I listen. There's a verse about a door in the hill with a key that's not a key. I don't know what that means. You look like you might.
Sing me that verse
She sings, badly, quietly. A brass key. A tenth mark. A door that drinks.
Tell the old man you learned it
She does. Bram says nothing for a long time, and then, "we hold".
Crane's got me. Properly. Crate, seal, the lot. He's holding me at his post till you come. He's very polite about it. I'd rather he hit me. What's it going to cost?
Pay the fine; release her
Crane accepts coin and notes it. Wren owes you, and hates it.
Let Crane hold her
A night in Crane's post. He reads her Schedule Four. She says it was worse than a cell.
I made money this month. Real money. I could buy a house in the town. A Hullfolk in a house. The town'd hate it. The old man'd hate it more. I want to do it just to see their faces. Tell me not to.
Don't; buy a boat
She buys a boat. A good one. She names it something rude, in Hullfolk.
Do it; I'll witness the deed
A Hullfolk in a house on Chapel Street. Cole sells it to her at a premium and is faintly impressed.
You're the first Keeper who's never asked me for a cut. Dray didn't either, but Dray didn't know. You know. That's either very honest or very stupid. I've decided it's honest. Don't ruin it.
I won't
"Good. Here's a fish. It's not a cut. It's a fish."
What would a cut be worth?
"Ruined it." She grins anyway, and names a figure, and you refuse it, and she grins wider.

If you go in the hill, I'm coming. Not for you. For the old man, who won't, and for Mirren, who shouldn't, and because I know the reeds and you don't. That's not a favor. That's the price of the others.
Come, then
"Right. Bring a lamp. Bring two."
Nobody's going in the hill
"Sure. Nobody. I'll bring two lamps anyway."
I hear the chest is light again. I do not hear things; I am told them, kindly, by people who owe me. My offer stands. My terms have not changed, which at this point is a kindness.
Borrow
Ten marks in, one in ten out, monthly. The bell on her door rings for you now.
Not from you
"From whom, then? I ask because I would like to buy their debt."
The chest cannot meet next watch's wages. For the record, the Company will advance them against the Keeper's own salary. For the record, that is not a kindness. It is a lien.
Take the advance
The hands are paid. You are not, for a season.
Pay them short and explain
Dace explains. Badly. The hands understand anyway, which is worse.
The hands drink on credit at my bar because you pay them late. I've carried it a month. I'm not a bank. I'm a reeve with a cellar. Who's paying, Keeper, you or the moot?
The Coffers, what there is
The chest empties into the inn. The hands are sober, briefly.
Cut the hands' credit
"Right. I'll tell them who said so."

Sorry. I know there's no money. The west paddle needs a new spindle or it needs a prayer. I've asked Hale for the prayer. She says the spindle's more reliable. I agree with her. I never agree with her.
The spindle, somehow
You sell the good chair. Cole buys it back for less than she gave it.
The prayer
Hale prays over the paddle. It runs another month. Nobody explains it.
Three things. Wages are two watches late. Two hands have gone down to Lock 6 where the Keeper pays. And the rest are asking me if I'm going too.
Sell the Company lamp oil
The town has oil for a month. Vosk will ask. Not yet.
Ask them to wait one more
"One more. Right. That's what I said last time."
Your chest is empty. Mine isn't. I'll pay a season's tolls in advance at face value, no discount, no conditions. I'm not being generous. I'm buying a Keeper who remembers who paid the wages.
Take the season
The chest is full of Sorrel coin. You remember.
No Keeper is for sale
"Everyone's for sale. Some of you just haven't seen the price yet."
Keeper, the Board has noticed the chest. The Board does not like noticing chests. There is a phrase in their letter, 'fiscal stewardship', which I have never seen used kindly.
Ask the Board for relief
Relief arrives: a loan at Company rates, and Vosk's closer attention.
Raise tolls until it recovers
Bargees pay more and say so. The chest breathes.
The chest has a false bottom you did not know about. Under it, twenty marks in old coin and a note in Dray's hand: 'For the day the Company stops paying. It will.'
Take it; the day has come
Twenty marks. The note goes in the Ledger.
Leave it; the day is not yet
You close the false bottom. You know it is there now, which is something.
You have missed a payment. I have sent no men; I said I would not. I have sent a note to the Company, as I said I would. Kindly expect a visitor.
Pay double now
The chest bleeds. The note is withdrawn, kindly.
Let the Company come
Vosk reads the note twice. "Noted. Irregular. Both of you."
The moot's had an idea. A town toll, on top of the Company's, for the town's own works. Collected at your gate, by your hands, into a chest that isn't yours. The Company would hate it.
Collect the town toll
Two chests on the sill. Bargees pay both, swearing. The town mends its roofs.
One toll, the Company's
"Thought so. Had to ask. The moot made me."
You have sold Company property to meet wages. I know because I know. For the record, I have not written it down. For the record, I am deciding whether to.
Write it down
"Noted. You are the first to say that." She writes less than she could.
Ask her not to
"I did not hear that. You will find I hear very well."
I've been paying for spindle oil myself. Roughly a mark a week. Sorry. I didn't want to add to the chest. I'm telling you now because I've run out too.
Pay her back, all of it
Six marks. She tries to refuse. She takes it.
Ask Tamm for tallow instead
Tallow. The gears run, greasy and slow. Quenn does not complain.
Two things. A bargee's offered to pay his toll in coal instead of coin, and the Company store'll take coal. And half the hands have no coal at home.
Coal to the hands
Warm houses, empty Book. Vosk notes a toll paid in 'kind'.
Coal to the store, coin to the chest
The store pays less than the toll was worth. The chest breathes anyway.

Delay costs, and so does poverty. I can put you in touch with a Sorrel banker who lends to Company posts against future tolls. It's legal. Barely. The Company would call it 'irregular'. The Company isn't broke.
Meet the banker
Sorrel gold in a Company chest. The paper is very long.
No Sorrel money
"Suit yourself. The Aldmere bankers won't call you either. They don't lend to canals."
Nothing in the chest but the chest. The hands know. The town knows. The Company will know on Tuesday. There is one thing left to sell, and it is the Keeper's own good name at the gate.
Sell precedence for a week
The queue reorders itself by coin. It is fast and ugly and pays the wages.
Go to the moot with empty hands
The town votes a levy on itself. For you. Nobody expected that.
The chest holds more than the toll table can produce. I have checked the table. I have checked the Book. For the record, one of them is wrong, and it is not the table.
Remit the surplus to Ardent
"Noted. Correct." The surplus goes east. The Book is honest again.
The Book is right
"Noted." She underlines something.
A full chest attracts attention. I would not dream of lending to you now; I would like to borrow. A small sum, at your terms, for a building. It would be kind. It would also be recorded.
Lend to Cole
The Company's money in Cole's building. It is the most irregular thing you have done.
The chest is the Company's
"Of course. I only wanted to hear you say it."
Word is the chest is full and the town's roofs are not. The moot's asked me to ask: is any of it the town's, or is it all going to Ardent to buy a Board member a launch?
Fund the roofs
Slate on every roof in the low street by winter. Vosk reads the entry twice.
It goes to Ardent
"Right. I'll tell them. I'll tell them the word 'launch', too."

There's money. There's actually money. Sorry, I've never said that before. I could rebuild the west paddle gear properly. Both sides. Marrow's pattern. It would take the whole surplus and it would last fifty years.
Marrow's pattern; the whole surplus
Six weeks. The gear runs like water. Vosk approves the spend without a word, which is unheard of.
Keep the surplus for a bad year
"Right. Sensible. Sorry. I'll patch it."
The chest is heavy. The hands know it's heavy because they carry it. And they've asked, politely, whether a heavy chest means a bonus or just a heavier chest.
A bonus
A mark a man. Ilse's takings double for a night.
A heavier chest
"Right. Just checking." They carry it anyway.
You're rich. Relatively. My principals would like to buy the summit's surplus lamp oil, rope and tallow at a premium. The Company will say its stores aren't for sale. The Company isn't here. I am.
Sell the surplus stores
The chest grows. The stores shrink. Winter is a way off.
Company stores stay
"Fine. I'll buy them from Lock 8. Tobin sells anything."
Keeper! The summit's accounts are the envy of the flight. The Board has asked how. I said 'the Meridian spirit'. They asked again. I would be grateful for a sentence I could send them.
Efficient tolling and dry weather
Pell sends it. Ardent accepts it. Vosk, reading the copy, does not.
Send them the Book
"The Book. Itself. Ah." He does not send it. He sends a summary.
The chest will not close. Coin on coin, scrip on scrip, and no honest line in the Book that adds to it. Whatever you have been doing, you have been doing well. Someone will ask.
Bury half in the false bottom
Dray's hiding place holds. Nobody has ever looked. Yet.
Spend it on the town, visibly
A new wharf crane. The town cheers. The Book cannot explain the crane.
A Board auditor from Ardent arrives Tuesday to count the chest against the Book. I would rather the count was right than that he found it wrong. For the record, this is not advice.
Make the Book right
Three nights of honest arithmetic. The count matches. He is faintly disappointed.
Let him find what he finds
He finds it. He is not disappointed. Vosk says nothing at all.
The town says the Keeper is rich. The town says it the way it said it of Dray, the month before he went. I am not warning you. I am a landlady. I am telling you what tenants say.
Ask what they said of Dray
"That he'd found something worth more than tolls. Kindly forget I repeated it."
Let them talk
"They will. They do. I collect it, like rent."
Somebody tried the toll chest last night with a bar. My potboy saw them off. Sorrel accent, he says. A full chest is a lit lamp, Keeper. Either spend it or guard it. Right now you're doing neither.
Post a guard
Dace's man sleeps on the chest. It is very uncomfortable and very safe.
Spend it down on the gates
New timber, new gear, and a chest no thief would bother with.
With this much in the chest I could hire a proper survey of the north bank. Sorrel engineers, not Company. I'd like to know what's under there. Sorry. I've wanted to know for six years.
Hire the survey
Sorrel engineers on the north bank for a week. Vosk watches them from the Company house.
The Company surveys its own bank
"It doesn't, though. That's rather the point. Sorry."
Three things. Vosk's counted the chest twice this week. Kell's coming. And the hands say if the Keeper's going to be arrested they'd like their bonus first.
Pay the bonus
Paid. The hands are loyal for a month, which is longer than most things.
Nobody is being arrested
"Right. I'll tell them that. They'll believe it about as much as I do."
I know where the surplus came from. On my shore nobody minds. On the other they mind a great deal. My principals could buy a 'consultancy' from you, papered and legal. It costs a favor later.
The consultancy
Paper covers coin. The favor is not named. It will be.
Let it stand
"Brave. Or slow. I'll find out which when Kell does."

Keeper, I have defended the summit's accounts to the Board with every adjective I possess. I am running out. Either the surplus goes to Ardent this week or I stop defending, and I have never stopped anything.
Send it to Ardent
The chest is honest and light. Pell finds new adjectives.
Stop defending
He stops. It is very quiet. Kell arrives on Tuesday.
Keeper. The Board's letters have stopped using my name. They use 'the summit'. When the Board stops using names it is preparing to change them. I say this as a friend, which I have never said before.
Ask what would restore their favor
"Figures. Silence. A Jubilee without incident. Any one of the three."
Let them change the names
"You do not mean that. I hope you do not mean that."
The Board has asked me whether the Keeper should be retained. For the record, I have not yet answered. For the record, I am not required to answer favorably. I am asking you for a reason to.
Give her the honest Book
She reads it all. "Noted. It will do." It does.
Give her the reason she wants to hear
"You do not know what I want to hear. Nobody does." She answers anyway. Neutrally.
The Board's view is that the summit has become 'a town post with a Company name'. The Board would like the name back. I am here to see whether the Keeper can return it, or whether someone else must.
The Company's gate, from today
Inspections, tolls, reports, all as written. The town notices at once.
The town is the gate
"The Board's view differs. Regrettably, so, in time, will your appointment."
COMPANY TO KEEPER STOP EXPLAIN IN WRITING WHY SUMMIT HAS DEPARTED FROM STANDING ORDERS ON FOUR OCCASIONS STOP REPLY BY RETURN STOP
Explain, at length
Nine pages. Fennick's hand aches. Ardent replies: 'NOTED'.
'THE GATE REQUIRED IT'
Five words. Silence for a week, then Vosk, at your door.
There's a wire come for Vosk about you. I didn't read it. I read it. It says 'PREPARE SUCCESSION'. I'm sorry. I thought you'd want to know before she did. She doesn't yet. She's at supper.
Go to Pell tonight
Pell, in his nightshirt, wires Ardent nine adjectives in your defense. It buys a month.
Let it come
"You're very calm. Dray was calm. Sorry. Sorry."
The Courier hears the Company wants you gone. The Courier's readers rather like you. A piece, 'THE KEEPER THE COMPANY FEARS', would make you very hard to dismiss and very easy to hate in Ardent.
Print it
You are famous for a week and unemployable in Ardent forever.
Don't
"Your funeral. Literally, possibly. I'll hold it."

I note that the Company appears displeased with you. I note also that the Compact provides for Aldmere to object to a Keeper's removal 'where the Keeper has upheld the Compact'. You have, mostly. Shall I object?
Object
Aldmere objects, formally. The Board is astonished. You are retained, resentfully.
Let the Company decide
"Duly. I shall note that you declined protection. It is unusual."

Sorry. If they dismiss you they'll send someone who does what they're told, and I'll be transferred, and the drawer will be emptied. I've copied everything. I'd like you to have the copies. Now, while you're still here.
Take the copies
A folio of figures, in her small hand. It is heavier than paper.
Keep them; you are safer than I am
"Am I? Oh. Yes. Roughly." She keeps them.

Keeper, a proposal. I write to the Board that the summit's irregularities were mine. Superintendent's discretion. It is nearly true. They will scold me. They have never dismissed a Superintendent. They dismiss Keepers.
Let him take it
He takes it. The Board scolds him for nine pages. He frames the ninth.
No; it was mine
"Magnificent. Foolish. I shall write to them anyway, more carefully."
I have written my recommendation. You will find it is not what the Board expects from me. You will also find I have not sent it. I am giving you one watch to make it true.
Ask what it says
"'Retain.' One word. It is more than I have written for anyone."
Send it as it is
"Noted." She sends it. It says retain. You did not deserve to know that.
COMPANY TO KEEPER STOP AUDITOR VOSK TO ASSUME JOINT AUTHORITY OVER GATE OPERATIONS PENDING REVIEW STOP ACKNOWLEDGE STOP
Acknowledge
Vosk at the gate beside you. She does not interfere. She watches.
Refuse joint authority
Fennick sends it with his eyes shut. Ardent does not reply. Vosk does not come.
The Board has drafted your dismissal. I have it here, undelivered, because the Board asked my view, and my view is that you are useful in a way the Board does not understand. Make me right.
Ask what would make him right
"Nothing dramatic. A quiet quarter. The Board forgets what is quiet."
Deliver it if you must
"Regrettably, I must not, yet. You are more stubborn than useful. It will do."

In strictest confidence, Keeper: I've been sending your figures to Ardent a little rounder than they are. Up. Not much. I thought it'd help. Now I don't know how to stop without it looking like they fell.
Stop; send the true figures
The figures fall on paper. Ardent asks why. You tell them the truth about Fennick, sparing him.
Keep rounding
"Right. Right. I'll round. I'm good at rounding."
I'm told Ardent has a replacement Keeper picked. Sorrel man. My readers would like to know what you'd say to him. I'd like to print it before he arrives so it's waiting for him.
'Watch the gauge'
The line is printed. The replacement never arrives. Nobody explains why.
Nothing for print
"Fine. I'll print that you said nothing. It reads as dignity."

I have been asked by Aldmere to report whether the Company's difficulties with its Keeper create 'an opportunity'. I have said I do not understand the question. I understand it. I am asking whether you want me to.
Aldmere's opportunity is mine
He reports carefully. Aldmere's interest in the summit sharpens.
Don't understand it
"Duly. I shall remain confused. It is restful."
Keeper! The Board has used your name. Favorably. In a minute. I have never been in a minute. They propose you attend the Jubilee dinner in Ardent as 'the face of the summit'. The face, Keeper!
Attend
A week in Ardent. Speeches. Your face on a program. The gate runs without you.
The gate needs its Keeper
"Modest. The Board does not reward modesty. I do, privately."
The Board trusts you. For the record, that is a dangerous position at this summit. The last Keeper they trusted this much was asked to do things that are not in the manual. You will be asked.
Ask what things
"Sign statements. Lose papers. Look elsewhere. Small things. They accumulate."
I will do what the Company needs
"Noted." A pause longer than her pauses. "Noted."
The Board has a task for reliable Keepers: sign, as witness, that the sluice house was inspected this quarter and found 'disused and sound'. It was not inspected. Sign anyway.
Sign
Your name on a lie about a building you have never entered.
Inspect it first
"Regrettably, the key is in Ardent." It is not. Vosk has it. You saw it.
COMPANY TO KEEPER STOP BOARD COMMENDS SUMMIT STOP KEEPER TO SUBMIT NAMES OF LOCK HANDS SUITABLE FOR REDUCTION STOP EFFICIENCY DIVIDEND STOP
Submit two names
Two men go down the flight. The Board's dividend arrives in scrip.
No names; all are needed
The commendation is quietly withdrawn from the minute.

You'll never guess. Ardent's asked me to wire them every visitor you receive. By name. In strictest confidence, they think you're going to be Superintendent and they want to know who you know. Should I?
Send the names
Ardent knows who drinks at your table. Some of them stop.
Send them nothing
"Right. I'll send them the weather. They like the weather."
COMPANY'S DARLING. That's the headline Sorrel wants. Aldmere wants COMPANY'S CREATURE. I've got both set. I'll run whichever you don't hate more, or neither if you give me something better.
Run 'Darling'
Sorrel laughs. Ardent is pleased. The town looks at you sideways.
Give him the water figures
He stops setting type. "These are real?" They are.

I note that the Company has begun addressing the Keeper as 'our representative at the summit'. The Compact recognizes a Keeper. It does not recognize a representative. I am concerned about whom I am dealing with.
You are dealing with the Keeper
"Duly. I shall hold you to that. It is a comfort to have something to hold."
The Company's representative
"Then I shall address my correspondence accordingly. It will be longer."

They've offered me a post in Ardent. Reservoirs. Sorry. Real reservoirs, with water in them. I think it's because you're in favor and they want your engineer where they can see her. I don't want to go.
Refuse it for her
You write to Ardent. She stays. Ardent remembers you kept her.
Real reservoirs are a gift
She goes. The drawer goes with her, emptied by Vosk first.
A delicate matter, Keeper. The Board is so pleased with you that it has asked whether I am necessary. I have been at this summit twenty years. I would like you to tell them I am.
Tell them he is
You write nine adjectives about Pell. He reads them and cannot speak.
Let the Board decide
"Ah." He does not say anything else for a week. The Board keeps him. Barely.
You are to be given a key. Not the gate keys. A brass one. For the record, I argued against it and was overruled. You will find the door it opens is one you have asked about.
Take the key
Brass, stamped S.H. Warm from her hand. She does not let go at once.
Refuse it
"Noted. That was wise. It will not be offered twice."

The Board would like the Keeper to address the Jubilee crowd on the Company's behalf. A short speech, prepared in Ardent. You need not read it beforehand. Regrettably, you need not understand it either.
Read the speech as given
The speech thanks 'the Ninefold Reservoirs'. Quenn, in the crowd, looks at her feet.
Write your own
You thank the hands and the water. Ardent notes the omission.
COMPANY TO KEEPER STOP BOARD PROPOSES KEEPER FOR SUPERINTENDENT ON PELL'S RETIREMENT STOP PELL NOT YET INFORMED STOP ADVISE STOP
Accept, and tell Pell yourself
He takes it beautifully. He does not mean a word of it.
Decline; Pell stays
Ardent is puzzled. Pell, learning of it from Fennick, is speechless for a day.
Ardent's sent a wire meant for the next Keeper. Instructions. It says the summit Keeper is 'not to be informed of the north bank works'. There aren't any north bank works. Are there?
Go and look tonight
Lamps below the sluice house. Men with picks. They do not see you. You hope.
Wire it on and forget it
"Right. Forgotten. I'm good at forgetting. I'm not, actually."

Ardent's asked me, through a friend of a friend, to write you up as the model Keeper. Paid. Handsomely. I've never been paid by a Company to praise anyone. I'm asking if you'd mind. I'd mind, a little.
Take their money; write the truth
He takes it and writes something honest. Ardent does not pay twice.
Write what they want
MODEL KEEPER. The town reads it aloud at the inn, in voices.
I note the Board has awarded you a medal. Aldmere has never recognized a Company medal. I have written suggesting it does, in your case. I do not know why I did that.
Thank him
"Do not. I shall regret it by Tuesday." He does not.
Withdraw the letter
"Very well. I note that I am relieved. And disappointed. Both, duly."
Nobody came to the moot. That's never happened. They didn't come because they've decided, and they don't need a moot to tell them. I came, because someone should tell you.
Ask what they decided
"That you're the Company's. That the Company's the flood. Work it out."
The moot is not my concern
"No. It'll be at your door, though. It'll bring lamps."
Three things. The hands won't take orders from the Keeper's mouth, only from mine. The town's stopped selling the lock house bread. And somebody's cut the tow rope on the Company boat. Clean.
Give orders through Dace
The gate runs on Dace's word. He does not enjoy it as much as you'd think.
The Keeper gives the orders
Orders are given. Some are obeyed. Slowly.
The town is angry with you, and angry towns pay late. I am owed by half of it. If the Keeper would like the town calmer, the Keeper could pay its debts to me. I would announce who paid. Kindly.
Pay the town's debts to Cole
You are, briefly, the most popular person in Halfway. Cole is the richest.
The town's debts are the town's
"Of course. Then it will remain angry, and I shall remain patient."
Someone has put a dead rat on the Keeper's step. Then another. Rats carry things, and the person doing it is a patient of mine. I will not say who. Stop giving them reasons.
Ask what reasons
"The Company's. Every day you do its work in its voice, the town hears it."
Find who did it
Dace finds him. It is Perrin. He has four children and a flooded cellar.
A child throws a stone at the Keeper's window and runs. The stone has a paper round it. The paper says GO HOME in a careful adult hand that has been to the town school.
Post the paper on the gate
The town reads its own handwriting. Some are ashamed. Some sign it.
Burn it; mend the window
Tamm mends the window and says nothing, which is a kindness.
The town wants you gone. That's a story. 'KEEPER BESIEGED', or 'TOWN TURNS ON ITS OWN KEEPER'. Victim or villain? I've got type for both.
'Besieged'
Sorrel pities you. The town hates being pitied more than it hates you.
Neither; print the water figures
He prints them. The town reads them. Something shifts, not toward you, but away from the Company.
They ran a Keeper out in my day. Year 44. Walked him to the stone with lamps, quiet as a funeral. He'd done nothing much, for too long. You've done more. Might not help.
Ask what would have helped him
"One thing they could see. One. Didn't have to be big."
Buy him a drink and say nothing
He drinks it. "Dray sat there too. Same face."
They're saying things about you at the inn. The things they said about him, before. I told them to stop. They told me I live in your house. I do. I'm asking if I should keep living in it.
Stay; it is your house
"It is." She stays. The inn talks about that too.
Go to Ilse's until this passes
She goes. The house is very quiet. The town approves of her, at least.
The moot met without me and voted to withhold the town's labor from the gate. No hands but the Company's. No repairs. No sandbags. I'm telling you as reeve. As Ilse, I'd have voted the same.
Requisition labor under the emergency clause
You compel the town. It comes, and it does not forget the compelling.
Work with the Company's hands alone
Dace and four men run a summit lock. The gate slows to a crawl.
Three things. The hands have been asked, by the town, to walk out. Half want to. And the half that don't have asked me to ask you for one reason to stay that isn't wages.
'Someone must watch the water'
Dace repeats it. It is not what they expected. They stay.
Wages are the reason
"Right." Half walk out. The other half work double.
If the town runs you out, the Keeper's house falls to me under the default clause. I would rather it did not. I am telling you so you know my interest is honest.
Ask her to speak at the moot
Cole speaks. The town listens to money. It buys a month.
Your interest is noted
"Kindly. I shall have the locks measured, just in case."
A man came to me with a broken hand from hitting the Company house door at night. Drunk and ashamed. He was not alone. There were eleven. I am telling you the number.
Open the Company house to the town
You hold a meeting in the Company's own parlor. Pell is appalled. The town is astonished.
Bar the door and post a guard
Dace's man on the step all night. Eleven becomes twenty.
The town has painted the boundary stone white and cleared the path to it. Nobody has said why. Everybody knows why. A child asks you, quite kindly, whether you will need a lamp for the walk.
'I hope not'
The child considers this and offers to lend you one anyway.
Have the stone repainted grey
It is white again by morning.

There's a petition going round for your removal. A hundred names. I've seen it. Half of them are in the same hand and that hand is Cole's clerk. I could print that. It would be very funny and very cruel.
Print it
The petition dies laughing. Cole does not speak to you for a month.
Leave the petition alone
"Merciful. Wasted, but merciful." A hundred names reach Ardent.
I've held them off a month. I can't hold them another. They want the Keeper at the moot tonight, to answer for the Company. Come, and they might not walk you out. I'm promising nothing.
Go to the moot
Three hours of shouting. At the end, nobody walks anywhere. It is not forgiveness. It is a start.
The Keeper does not answer to moots
"Then get your lamp."
They've started calling it 'the Keeper's gate' at the inn. Not the Company's. Yours. It's meant kindly. I've been reeve long enough to know what kindly turns into when the Company hears it.
Let them call it what they like
The name sticks. Vosk hears it. She writes it down.
It is the Company's gate
"Say it at the inn, then. Loud. They need reminding, for their own good."
The hands have made you a sign for the gate. It says KEEPER'S LOCK. They want to hang it over the Company's. And Pell's coming Thursday.
Hang it
KEEPER'S LOCK over MERIDIAN CANAL COMPANY. Pell sees it Thursday and goes a color.
Hang it in the lock house, inside
Inside. The hands are pleased anyway. Pell never sees it.
The town loves you. I have watched towns love people; it is expensive. They will ask for things and remember every refusal. I would like to be your first refusal. I am asking for nothing.
Then you have it
"Kindly. Now everyone else knows you can say no. You owe me."
I will refuse when I must
"Everyone says that. Everyone is wrong. Kindly."

You are the most popular Keeper in eighty years and you look worse than any of them. Popularity is a symptom. The town wants you at every bedside, every wedding, every moot. Stop going to some of them.
Stop going to some
You miss a wedding. The couple forgives you. You sleep.
The town needs its Keeper
"Its Keeper needs a liver. I am a physician, not a friend, but I am also that."
A deputation from the town: they would like the Keeper to stand for reeve. Ilse has said she'd step aside. The Company forbids Keepers from holding town office. The Company has not been asked.
Stand
You are reeve and Keeper. The Company learns from the Courier.
Ilse is the reeve
The deputation goes away pleased anyway. Ilse is quietly relieved.
THE TOWN THAT LOVES ITS KEEPER. It's a lovely piece. It's also the kind of piece that gets read in Ardent as THE KEEPER WHO LOVES THE TOWN, which is a different piece. Shall I run it?
Run it
The town frames it. Ardent files it under something else.
Run something about the water instead
He runs the gauge figures with no headline. It is the quietest thing he has ever printed. Ardent notices anyway.
They loved a Keeper once, in Year 44. Rose for him when the Company crossed him. Company hanged three men for it. Him they sent east. Love's a thing to be careful with.
Ask what he'd have done
"Told them to sit down before they stood up. He didn't. He liked being loved."
The town can stand if it likes
"It can. It'll stand on you."
They like you. The town. They didn't like him; they respected him, which is different. I don't know which is better. I know which one they'd fight for. Would you let them?
Never
"Good. He'd have said that." She almost smiles.
If it came to it
"Then it will. Things do, here."
The moot voted last night. Not about you. For you. They've voted the town won't obey any Company order the Keeper hasn't signed. I said that's sedition. They said it's loyalty. It's both.
Ask them to rescind it
They rescind, sulking. Ardent never hears. You breathe.
Let it stand
It stands. Fennick wires it to Ardent before you can stop him. He thought you'd be pleased.
Three things. A Company inspector came to count the hands and the hands wouldn't be counted without the Keeper present. He left. Ardent's wired. And the hands think it was funny.
Be present for the recount
You stand there while a small man counts eleven people. Nobody laughs. Nearly.
It was funny
"It was." Ardent does not think so.
Tenants are refusing rent 'until the Keeper says'. I have never needed a Keeper's leave to collect rent. I am asking politely. I have other ways of asking.
Tell them to pay
They pay. They also learn you and Cole are on the same side, which you are not.
The rent is between you and them
"Then the buildings are between me and the Company. Kindly."
Men at the inn last night were talking about the Company house and what burns. I did not think they meant it in Year 44 either. You are the only one they will listen to.
Go to the inn tonight and speak
You speak. They listen, sullenly, and put down whatever they were holding.
Send Dace
Dace goes. He is one of them. He comes back quiet.
A crowd at the gate, cheerful, with a barrel. They have come to carry the Keeper shoulder-high round the town for no reason anyone can give. The Company house windows are all lit and all watching.
Be carried
Round the town twice. Vosk, at her window, does not close the curtain.
Stand them a drink instead
They drink. They carry Dace instead, who hates it.
My son died the week after the town rose for a Keeper. I've never told you that. I'm telling you because the town's about to do it again and I'd rather bury you than another boy. Stop them.
Stop them
You stand on the wharf and tell the town to go home. It does, for you. Only for you.
I cannot stop them
"You can. You won't. It's the same thing when there's a lamp in the window."
Ardent has a word for a post whose town obeys the Keeper over the Company: sedition. It's in a wire I've seen, with your name in it. I'd like to print it. You'd like me not to.
Print it
The town reads that it is seditious and is delighted. Ardent is not.
Hold it
"Held. For now. I hold things about a month."
The queue reaches Lock 7. Bargees have stopped shouting and started cooking. Somebody has set up a stall selling tea to the line. Somebody else is selling places in it.
Work the gate through the night
Lamps, paddles, tired hands. The queue shortens by a third.
Ban the place-selling
The seller moves down to Lock 8 and sells from there.
Nine days. Nine. My principals have coal rotting in the pound. Rotting. It doesn't, but it feels like it does. Waive inspections for a week and I'll clear my boats myself, in order, quietly.
Waive for a week
Sorrel's fleet clears in three days. Crane records every one.
Inspections stand
"Then my boats stand too. All of them. In your pound."
The queue is long, and I am part of the reason. The Compact permits one inspection in three when trade is 'materially impeded'. I have never invoked it. I am invoking it.
One in three
"Duly." The queue moves. He looks faintly ill at the boats he did not open.
Inspect them all; I will wear it
"I note that. I note it with something like respect."
Keeper, the Courier has a drawing of the queue with my face on every boat. Every boat. The Board has seen it. I would like to see boats move. I would like it more than I have ever liked anything.
Suspend the toll for a day
Free passage. The pound empties like a bath. The chest does not fill.
Boats move when they move
"When they move. Yes. A philosophy, Keeper. The Board does not have one."
Bargees in the queue have started fighting over places. Two knives so far. My men could keep order on the towpath. It is not our job. It is nobody's job. That is the problem.
Ask his men to keep order
Armed Sorrel men on a Company towpath. Order is kept. Crane writes a very long letter.
Dace and the hands keep order
The hands do it, badly, and are not paid for it.
Double watches, Keeper. One hand's fallen asleep on the beam and nearly gone in. And the queue's started calling us 'the Halfway sleepers'.
Hire day labor from the queue
Bargees turn paddles for their own boats. It is chaos and it works.
Rest the hands; the queue waits
A day lost. Nobody falls in.

Nine boats back there are Hullfolk with nothing aboard that matters. Let them go round by the Reach channel, the shallow one, and your queue's a third shorter by dark. Nobody has to know they didn't pay.
The Reach channel
Nine boats vanish from the queue. The Book does not notice.
Everyone through the gate
"Fair. Slow, but fair. I'll tell them you said fair."
THE GREAT HALFWAY JAM. Front page, both shores. I'm not asking permission; I'm asking for the Keeper's own explanation, verbatim, so it's fair. You get one paragraph.
Blame the water
'KEEPER: THE POUND IS FAILING.' Ardent reads it before breakfast.
Blame the season
'KEEPER BLAMES WEATHER.' It is what everyone expected.
An Aldmere grain fleet, twelve boats, five days in the queue, and the master says the grain is heating in the holds. Heating grain is a fire waiting. He would like to go first.
Grain first
Twelve boats through. Coal bargees throw things. The grain does not burn.
Unload the hot holds on the wharf
Grain on the wharf, cooling. The town eats well for a week.
I've done your sums. If you run the gate on the Sorrel pattern, two boats a filling, nose to tail, you double throughput. The Company forbids it. The Company isn't standing in a nine-day queue.
Two boats a filling
Doubled. Fast. Hulls kiss twice. Nothing breaks. Yet.
One boat, as written
"Fine. I'll write to the Board about the pattern. In my hand. With your name."
A Sorrel vessel in the queue has struck an Aldmere vessel deliberately. Both captains claim the other. Under the Compact I must hold both until a magistrate arrives. A magistrate is nine days away.
Hold both
Two boats in the pound for nine days. The queue behind them ages.
Fine both, release both
"Irregular. Efficient. I shall record my disapproval and my relief."

A thought, Keeper. A magnificent one. We open the disused side-pond and float the smaller boats round the chamber entirely. Quenn says the side-pond gates have not moved since Year 31. Quenn says a lot of things.
Open the side-pond
The gates move, groaning. Small boats go round. The pound drops a mark for the water it took.
Quenn is usually right
"Usually. Yes. A word the Board does not like."
My convoy has waited six days and my men have behaved. When we go through, we go through together and nobody boards us. That is not a request either.
Together, uninspected
The convoy passes as a unit. Crane records a Compact breach in beautiful handwriting.
Together, inspected
"Understood." It is not a happy word.
Three things. Aldmere's closed its flight below for 'repairs' because our queue's backing into their pounds. Nothing can leave the summit going east. And the Sorrel boats are laughing.
Wire Aldmere; demand they open
They open in two days. Crane, embarrassed, says nothing about it.
Send everything west instead
Westbound only. Sorrel stops laughing when its pounds fill.
Somebody in the queue is selling a story that the gate's slow because the Keeper takes coin to move boats up. It's not true. I'd know. But I could make it true, and then it'd be a fast queue.
Kill the story
Wren kills it. You do not ask how.
Let the queue believe it
Coin arrives. Boats move. Vosk, later, has questions.
Forty boats through since dawn and the chamber has not been empty once. Hulls are touching in the approach. A bargee has been knocked into the pound by his own tiller and fished out laughing.
Slow it down
The hands breathe. The bargees complain. Nobody goes in the water.
Keep the pace; it is a record
A record. The gate rattles like a mill.
This is more like it. My principals are delighted. They'd like to be more delighted. Night passages, no inspections, two boats a filling. All three and I'll name a barge after you.
All three
The gate runs day and night. A barge called *Keeper* goes east. Crane goes pale.
None; it is fast enough
"Fast enough. There's no such thing. Fine."
Four vessels inspected today, of the sixty that passed. Four. Under the Compact I am entitled to inspect any. I am entitled, not able. I am asking you to make me able.
Hold every fifth boat for him
"Duly. Thank you." He inspects with a thoroughness that is almost joy.
Inspect what you can
"I note that. I note that four is not what I can. Four is what I did."
Magnificent! Sixty-one vessels! The Board has wired congratulations, Keeper, actual congratulations, eleven words. I have had them framed. Can we do seventy?
Seventy
Seventy-two. The lower gate takes a hull in the face and holds. The town does not sleep.
Sixty-one is enough
"Enough. A word I have never framed."
Boats are going through at night with no lights and no questions. Some of them are mine. Some of them are not, and I do not know whose. That should worry you more than it worries me. It worries me.
Lights and names, or no passage
The night boats thin out. One does not come back for its name.
Night is night
"So it is. I'll double my own watch. You might too."
Three things. The hands are turning paddles so fast the gear's smoking. Two men have burns. And a coal barge came in so hot she's put her bow through the top gate's fender.
Stop for repairs
Half a day. New fender. The hands sit down for the first time in a week.
Work round it
The fender hangs by a bolt. The next barge takes it off.
With the gate running like this nobody's looking at anything. I moved four crates last night without trying. I'm telling you because if I can, anyone can, and I know who anyone is.
Who?
"Sorrel men who aren't Solas's. Coming east. Not with coal."
Slow the gate
"Sensible. Cost me money. Still sensible."
HALFWAY FLIES. Both shores. Sorrel loves you. Aldmere's Guilds say you're running a Sorrel gate. I've got a follow-up piece: 'What Is the Summit Not Inspecting?' I'd love a denial.
Deny it
'KEEPER DENIES.' Which is, in newspapers, a confession.
Give him an inspection to watch
Crane inspects a coal barge for the press. It is the happiest day of his year.
Two barges have entered the chamber at once, from opposite ends, because both bargees were told 'go' by different hands. They have stopped a yard apart. Both are shouting. The water is still rising.
Drop the water; back one out
An hour, some paint, and a bargee who will never trust a hand again.
Fill and pass both together
They rise together, a yard apart, glaring. It works. Nobody will admit it worked.
My competitor's boats are through in an hour and mine in two because your hands know his bargees. I'm not accusing anyone. I'm offering a standing gratuity to the hands. Call it a wage supplement.
Accept for the hands
The hands are paid twice. Sorrel coal moves first. Aldmere notices.
No gratuities at the gate
"Fine. Then I'll pay the other man's bargees to be slower."
I have counted. Of the vessels passed this week, eleven carried cargo that under Schedule Four required my seal. None had it. I am reporting to Aldmere. I am telling you first, which I need not.
Hold the next eleven
The gate slows to a crawl. Crane seals things with visible satisfaction.
Report what you must
"I shall. I note that you did not ask me not to."
A word, Keeper. The Board is pleased with the figures and displeased with the letters. Aldmere's Guilds. Something about the Compact. I need the figures to stay and the letters to stop. Manage it.
Restore inspections quietly
The figures dip. The letters stop. Pell notices the dip.
The figures are what matter
"Yes. Yes. That is what I said. Isn't it?"
One of the night boats had a man aboard I knew from the coalfield shooting. Not a coal man. Whatever is coming east is coming through your gate at speed. Slow it, or don't.
Slow it
The night boats stop. Some of them go round by the Reach. Wren says nothing.
The gate is not a border
"It's the only one there is."
We've passed more boats this month than in any month in the Book. The pound's down four marks for it. And the hands have asked, politely, what happens when there's no water left to pass them on.
Tell them the truth: I don't know
"Right. Honest. They'll take honest."
The reservoirs will make it up
"Right." He does not believe you. Neither do you.
A boat has gone through so fast it left its bargee on the wharf. He stands there with a rope in his hand, watching his barge go down the flight alone.
Send a boat after it
The barge is caught at Lock 8 by Tobin, who has been waiting for something like this for years.
The bargee's problem
He walks down the towpath after it. He does not come back up.
The gauge is at the sixth mark and dropping. Heavy barges are scraping the sill going in. The sound carries to the town, and the town has started to listen for it.
Halve the passages
Fewer boats, less lost to the flight. The queue grows.
Keep the boats moving
Every filling costs a finger of water. You can hear it.

Sorry. At this level the aqueduct should be making up the difference. It isn't. It can't. I've written to Ardent for the reservoir figures. They said the figures are 'in preparation'. For eighty years.
Write again, over my name
The reply comes to Vosk instead, and Vosk comes to you.
Work with what we have
"Which is the pound. Which is falling. Yes."
The Reach is on its side in the mud. We have moved the old and the children to the town's bank, where the town does not want them. We ask the gate for water. We know it cannot give it.
Close the gate two days
The pound rises a mark. The Reach floats. Pell counts the lost boats.
Open the town's wharf to them
Forty Hullfolk on the town wharf. Ilse manages it. Barely.
The well's dry. Not low. Dry. The brewery's stopped and the town's drinking Sorrel beer at Sorrel prices and blaming you. The well's never been dry before. Not in eighty years.
Ask why a well follows a pound
"Because it's the same water. Everyone knows that. Nobody says it."
Pay for the town's beer
The Coffers buy Sorrel beer. Nobody is happy, but nobody is thirsty.
Nine nights of the Lamp Vigil and the water has not answered. The town is looking at me in a way it has not before. I would keep a tenth night. Stand with me.
Stand with her
A tenth night. The town sees the Keeper and the chaplain together. It helps them, if not the pound.
Nine is enough
"Then we shall tend what remains." She keeps the tenth alone.
Three things. A coal barge is aground on the sill. The bargee wants us to drag her off with the hands. And Quenn says dragging will take the sill's facing stones with her.
Drag her off
She comes off. So do three facing stones. Quenn does not speak to you for a day.
Unload her where she lies
A day of coal by hand. The sill lives. The bargee curses everyone.

Low water shows the gate's underside for the first time in years. She's rotten to a hand's depth. I can sister the timbers while she's exposed, if you close for three days. You'll never get another look.
Three days
The gate is sistered. It will outlast the pound.
We cannot spare three days
"No. Nobody ever can. That's how they rot."
It was this low the month before he went. He stood at the gauge every night. I asked him what he was looking at. He said 'the tenth mark'. I didn't know what he meant. I do now.
Show me the tenth mark
Below the sill line, painted over. She scrapes it clean with a knife.
Don't stand at the gauge
"I know. I know. I'm asking you not to either."
Cracked mud along the Reach where there was water a month ago. In the mud, exposed for the first time in eighty years: cut stone. A channel. Straight as a rule, running north into the bank.
Follow the channel
It runs to the sluice house and under it. You are not the first to follow it; there are old bootprints, dried in.
Cover it before the Company sees
You cover it. You do not know why. Bram, watching, nods once.
Another three marks and the chamber won't float a loaded barge. I can pump from the Reach end by hand, every hand we have, for maybe a week. It buys time. Nothing else.
Pump
A week of pumping. The pound falls anyway, slower.
Save the hands for the gates
"Right. Sorry. Right."
When the pound was this low in the Dry Year our grandmothers saw the channel and knew it. They said nothing, because they were afraid. We are less afraid. We ask the gate if it has seen the channel.
I have seen it
"Then you know where the water goes in. Now you must decide what to do about knowing."
I have seen mud
"Mud. Yes. Our grandmothers said mud too."
The moot voted. The town wants the gate closed until the pound comes back, and the Company can whistle. I voted against, for what it's worth. It's worth less than it was.
Close the gate for the town
Closed. Pell is apoplectic. The town brings you soup.
The gate stays open
"Right. I'll tell them. They'll remember I told them."
The undercroft is dry, Keeper. For the first time since I came. There are things in the far corner I have never reached. I am not sure I should be the one.
Go down with her
A chest. Letters, water-stained but legible. An engineer's hand.
Leave the corner
"Yes. Perhaps some things are meant to stay under water."
Three things. Vane's offering the hands double to pass her coal at this level. Crane says any passage at this level breaks the Compact's safety clause. And the hands would like the double.
Pass the coal
Coal through. Hands paid. Crane files. The sill takes another stone.
Safety clause holds
"Right. I'll tell the hands. They'll want to know who Crane is."
Pell wants a false floor in the chamber to raise the boats. It'd work for a week. Then it'd float, with a boat on it. I'll build it if you sign. I'd rather you didn't.
Sign for it
It works for a week. Then it floats. Nobody is aboard. Just.
Don't build it
"Good." Pell finds something else to be magnificent about.
Water over the towpath. The horses are up to their hocks and refuse the tow. Boats are drifting in the pound with nobody to pull them. The chapel undercroft has a foot in it.
Run every paddle down the flight
The pound falls. Lock 8 floods instead. Tobin sends word: 'about time'.
Sandbag the town first
The town works all night. The pound does not fall. It waits.
The east embankment's seeping. Not leaking, seeping. It does that above the seventh mark. I've never seen it above the eighth. Sorry. I'm telling you what I'd want to be told.
Shore the embankment
Stone, timber, every hand. The seep slows.
Drop the pound instead
"Yes. That's the other way. The flight won't like it."
High water. The Reach floats high and easy and our children swim where the mud was. We are the only ones glad. We know it. We ask the gate to remember that when it is asked to drain us.
Drain slowly
The pound comes down over a week. The Reach settles gently.
The town comes first
"It always has. We remember that too."
Two feet in my cellar. Every barrel afloat. The moot wants the paddles run and the moot wants to know why they weren't run yesterday. So do I. I'm the moot.
Run them now; apologize
The paddles run. The cellar drains. She does not accept the apology; she notes it.
The flight was full
"The flight. Your Company's flight. My cellar."
The undercroft is under water to the third step. There are things down there the water should not have. I have never asked a Keeper for anything. I am asking for the paddles.
The paddles, now
The undercroft drains over two days. She goes down alone with a lamp.
Ask what things
"The founding papers. Letters. Nothing that concerns the gate." Everything concerns the gate.
Water's over the top gate's sill when she's shut. That means she's not shut. That means anything in the chamber's going down the flight whether we like it or not.
Clear the chamber; nothing passes
No boats. The chamber is a waterfall for a day.
Pass boats on the flood
Boats go down fast. Very fast. One bargee will not do it again.

The Reach's stage is under and my yard's under and there's a Company barge come loose that's going to take my slipway with it unless somebody gets a line on her. Somebody with a boat. I've got a boat.
Go with him
Two hours in a rowing boat in a flood. The barge is saved. So is the slipway.
Let the barge go
It takes the slipway. Tamm rebuilds. He does not ask you for help.
He hated high water more than low. Low, you can see what's wrong. High, it's all underneath. He'd walk the embankment at night with a lamp. I've been doing it. I found a place that's soft.
Show me
The east bank, below the chapel. Your boot sinks to the ankle.
Tell Quenn, not me
"I did. She said 'sorry' and went white."
The overflow weir is roaring. It has not roared in living memory. Old Tobin has come up from Lock 8 to hear it and stands on the bank with his hat off, as if at a grave.
Ask him what he hears
"The Dry Year, backwards. Water going where it shouldn't."
Get him off the bank
You walk him to the inn. He is shaking, and not from the cold.
This is interesting. Sorry, wrong word. This is alarming. The pound's rising faster than rain and aqueduct together could fill it. Something else is putting water in. Something under the north bank.
Find the inflow
You find it in the dark: a boil of water off the sluice house, brown with hill-silt.
Drop the pound; ask later
"Later. Yes. There's always a later, until there isn't."
Our old singer says the hill is giving back what it took. She says it every high water. This time the young ones are listening. We ask the gate whether it wants them to.
Let them listen
The Song is sung on the Reach for three nights, all its verses.
Keep them at the pumps
"The pumps. Yes. The charter men would say the pumps."
The town's on the embankment with lanterns and no plan. Half want to cut the west bank to drain into the Reach. Half know that's murder. I need the Keeper to say which half, out loud, now.
Nobody cuts the west bank
You say it loud. Bram, at the back, hears it too.
Cut it; save the town
The Reach floods to the gunwales. Nobody drowns. Nobody forgets.
The flood has scoured the path and uncovered the founding stone at the chapel gate. There is a name on it that is not in any hymn. I have covered it. Leave the cloth.
Leave the cloth
The cloth stays. You have read the name already. Marrow.
Lift it
"Ysolde Marrow, who gave the water." Hale watches you read it and does not stop you.

Three things. Pell wants boats through on the high water because it's 'free lift'. Every boat we pass drops the pound a finger, which we want. Every boat we pass in this current is a coffin, which we don't.
Pass them; free lift
Nine boats down in a morning. One hits the lower gate. The gate wins.
Nothing moves on this current
Pell sulks. Dace nods. The pound falls on its own by evening.
The pound is a lake. The town's lower street is a canal. Children are being ferried to school on a door. Somebody has painted 'HALFWAY UNDER' on the Company house, and nobody has painted over it.
Leave the sign
It becomes the town's joke, then its name for the year.
Paint over it
It reappears by morning, larger.
